newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HKMA injects HK$200 mln into interbank market.
newsitem.headline: HKMA injects HK$200 mln into interbank market.

text.p: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), the territory's de facto central bank, said it injected HK$200 million into the interbank market Monday morning in view of the tight liquidity of the Hong Kong dollar.
"This is due to the IPOs (initial public offerings of new shares)," HKMA spokesman Osbert Lam said by telephone.
This was the third injection following Thursday and Friday last week, he added.
The HKMA injected HK$100 million and HK$107 million into the market, respectively, on Thursday and Friday.
A number of IPOs are being launched in Hong Kong and have tightened short-term Hong Kong dollar funding.
